title: The shape of a week
hook: worship, rest, friends, fast, feast, give
tomorrow: which month won't leave any room unless you plan it early?

segments.voice: Yesterday, reconciliation: leave the gift, go first, as much as lies in you. Your line was first be reconciled. Today, all the week's pieces on one page.

A calendar app shows a week as a grid: meetings, errands, a dentist appointment, a pickup. Nothing on the grid says what the week is for. Take a pen instead and draw seven boxes by hand. The pen drags a little on the paper; the lines come out crooked. Then, one by one, the boxes fill with the practices of these past days, and something shows up that no single box could show: a shape.
screen: `A GRID OF ERRANDS.` → `SEVEN BOXES, BY HAND.` → `SOMETHING SHOWS UP: A SHAPE.`

segments.voice: Ecclesiastes has the line for it, in the King James Bible: “To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven.” Here are the purposes. Worship, where the line was gather: people around word and table. A sabbath: rest is holy, made for people. A small group: two or three. A fast day: small, quiet, safe. A shared meal: break bread, and leave a chair for someone. A letter: encourage, by naming what you've seen. A creation walk: consider the lilies. A generous act, planned in the heart. And the weekly check: first be reconciled. Now look at the page, because pairs are hiding on it. A fast and a feast. Quiet and company. Receiving rest and giving gifts. Looking up at the sky and looking across at a person. Saying sorry and saying thank you. The shape isn't a checklist to pass. If a box goes empty, the week isn't ruined; you start again at the next one, the way the day's rhythm worked. That's why the line says grace: a gift, not a grade. And something to tell a friend tonight: every one of those boxes came from a text, not an app.
screen: `A TIME TO EVERY PURPOSE.` · `NINE PRACTICES, ONE PAGE.` · `PAIRS: FAST AND FEAST.` · `A GIFT, NOT A GRADE.` · then, large: `A WEEK OF GRACE.`

segments.voice: With a pen, draw seven boxes on a page and put one of these practices in each, wherever it fits your real week. Leave a box empty if nothing fits yet, and put a small mark where a fast sits next to a feast. Go slowly, and listen to the scratch of the pen as the shape comes in.
The shape of a week. Worship, rest, friends, fast, feast and giving, drawn on one page, held loosely, and kept by grace.
screen: `THE SHAPE OF A WEEK — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: a week of grace. Crooked boxes count; the shape is the gift. Day 1705, drawn.

screen: `DAY 1705 COUNTS.` → `LIVING IT · 24 OF 70.` → `TOMORROW: WHICH MONTH WON'T LEAVE ROOM UNLESS YOU PLAN IT?`

howItsDone: Some Christians keep a written rule of life, a simple weekly plan that sets times for worship, rest, prayer with others, fasting, shared meals and giving, and revisit it when life changes.
